title: Git and reproducible experiments
description: Record enough context to understand and repeat an experiment.
objectives: Review and commit a focused change
Connect a result to code, data, and configuration versions
explanation: Git records snapshots of tracked files. The working tree holds your current edits; the staging area selects what goes into the next commit. Use git status and git diff to inspect changes, then stage named files and inspect git diff --cached before committing.

A commit alone does not reproduce an AI experiment. Also record a data version or content hash, dependency versions, model identifier, configuration, evaluation cases, and random seeds where supported. External services and hardware can introduce variation even with the same seed.

Keep secrets, private datasets, generated caches, and large model files out of ordinary source commits. An ignore rule prevents accidental addition of untracked files; it does not remove files already tracked or erase history. Store a small experiment manifest beside a measured result so someone else can identify its inputs.

terms.definition: A recorded snapshot linked to repository history.
The selected changes prepared for the next commit.
A record of the inputs and settings needed to identify an experiment.

example: Experiment E12 compares two chunk sizes on the same ten questions. Its manifest records the code commit, document snapshot hash, embedding model version, chunk settings, and metrics. A changed source document becomes a new experiment input even if the code stays unchanged.
mistakes: Assuming a seed controls a remote service.
Keeping results without identifying the input dataset.
exercise: Create a small local repository with a script and an experiment manifest. Make one change, inspect the staged diff, and commit it. Write what another person would still need to reproduce the output.

questions.question: What does the Git staging area control?
questions.answer: It selects the changes included in the next commit.
questions.distractor: It automatically backs up every file on the computer.

questions.question: Which command reviews changes selected for a commit?
questions.answer: git diff --cached shows the staged changes before committing.
questions.distractor: git push displays only unstaged changes.

questions.question: A model alias changes behind the same name. Is the experiment fully pinned?
questions.answer: No. Record a resolved model version or acknowledge that the provider can change it.
questions.distractor: Yes, a name always identifies immutable weights.

questions.question: Why is a commit insufficient for experiment reproducibility?
questions.answer: Data, dependencies, configuration, external models, and environment can also affect results.
questions.distractor: Code cannot influence AI experiment results.

questions.question: Will adding a tracked secret to .gitignore erase it from history?
questions.answer: No. Revoke the credential and follow an appropriate repository cleanup procedure.
questions.distractor: Yes, ignore rules rewrite all prior commits.
